utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Do you think we have the next witness, Mr. Whiting?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm quite certain we do. The next witness is Lieutenant Ramadan Behluli.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KHAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to apologise. Before the witness is called there appears to be a technical problem with our headphones. Perhaps you can hear the static, but there's no control at all. So perhaps that can be sorted out.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Perhaps change the channels.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sounds like it's raining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to take the card and read the affirmation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will tell the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth. I swear by my flag.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Please sit down. We are going to proceed with your evidence now, and Mr. Whiting will ask you some questions. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir. Could you please state your name.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Ramadan Behluli.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, as you know, I will be asking questions in English and they will be translated for you into Albanian and you can respond to the questions in Albanian. If at any point you have trouble understanding the translation or understanding my questions, please tell me. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Sir, are you a lieutenant in the TMK in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. I am is sergeant in the ceremonial battalion of the Kosova troops.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Just so I get the title right, is it lieutenant or sergeant?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Lieutenant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you. Lieutenant, did you receive a subpoena from this Court requiring you to appear here today to testify?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I received a subpoena, a binding one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And this was a subpoena from the Court. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You understand that everyone present here, the Prosecutor, the Defence lawyers, and even the Judges if they so desire, will have an opportunity to ask you questions and that your job here is simply to answer the questions and to tell the truth. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On the 25th of April of 2003 did you receive a summons to attend an interview with the Office of the Prosecutor in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you attend that interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you tell the truth in that interview?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I did my best.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Have you -- were you given a transcript of the interview afterwards?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: They did, but rather late I would say. But I have some critical remarks about the transcript. Sometimes they have -- there is more than I have said, sometimes there is less, and sometimes things are not the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In particular, did you notice some mistakes relating to names of villages?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. Some sentences are not exactly the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Aside from the criticisms that you have mentioned, is the transcript substantially accurate?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Not accurate. That's why I said there are some shortcomings I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. Well, there is a recording of the interview, so if there are any issues related to that interview we can always have an opportunity to consult the recording. I'll ask you some more questions about this topic later, but I just want to ask you one thing. Were you injured during the war?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was the date of the injury, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how long -- as a result of this injury, how long were you away from battle?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I wasn't away for long. I went to see the doctor, to treat -- to have the wound treated, and then I went back to the position.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember what date you got back to the position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I think it was the 19th or the 20th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us where on your body you were injured? What kind of injury did you receive?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: On my right side.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: On your arm or your leg?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: My arm.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And, sir, did this injury have an effect on you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Not very much so I would say, but the consequences I suffered were during the war. I saw horrors, I saw a lot of bad things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. And was that -- were you traumatised by that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, I'm going to ask you some background questions first. Can you tell us your date of birth?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: 15 March 1960.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What village were you born in?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Zemun village in the vicinity of Belgrade where my parents were working then. That's where I was born. But now I am in -- I live in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How old were you when you began living in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I told you that very soon we moved away. I told you I opened my eyes in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, that -- the translation didn't capture that.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After two or three or maybe five days, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. And have you -- since then, have you always lived in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, how many years of education did you have?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I finished the primary school in the village, the high school in Ferizaj, and the first school of the higher school in Ferizaj again.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What year was that that you did the first year of higher school in Ferizaj?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you do your military service in the former Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What year was that?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did you serve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: In Bosnia, in Derventa for six months -- eight months and six months in Banja Luka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, are you married?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I am.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you have children?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I have two sons and two daughters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You told us you're presently a lieutenant in the ceremonial guard of the TMK. I'm not sure, did you tell us where that is based?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It is based in between Fushe Kosove and Pristina, in the barracks of Adem Jashari.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Have you been in the TMK since the end of the war, 1999?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, right from the first moment it was established and today.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before the war did you spend any time outside of -- living outside of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: For three years I was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What years were those?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What were you doing in Germany?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I worked for some time in a park and most of the time I worked in a factory.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when in 1997 you returned to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I think it was the 5th of May.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you return to your village in Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you live in Carraleve today?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No, I live in Ferizaj. I settled there after the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I want to draw your attention to your village in 1997/1998. Was Carraleve a mixed Albanian/Serb village, or was it only Albanian?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't ever remember to have seen someone other than Albanians there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us what other villages are around Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Petrastica, Zborce, Dulje, Rance, Belince.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where did the nearest Serbs live in 1997/1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: In Shtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you returned in 1997 in May, were you employed?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No, I was not employed, not in the village but only in Germany as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you return to Kosovo in 1997?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I couldn't stand it anymore in Germany. I was alone. My family was in Kosova. That's why I returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. Before the war did you have any problems with the Serb authorities? And I'm talking about now 1997 and the beginning of 1998.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I went to Germany because Serb police forces several times asked about me; that's why I left.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know why they were asking about you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The pretext was arm possession. Their policy was to strike fear among the population for the population to leave the place.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Before you went to Germany in 1994, were you ever arrested or detained by the Serb police?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No. But they did arrest me in 1997 and beat me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When in 1997 did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It was after May, in June I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Where were you arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I was at my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you given a reason for being arrested?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I tried not to be seen by them, to hide, to keep a low profile. But when they wanted to take away my sons, I surrendered -- I mean, I gave up to them. I mean, the pretext for them to look for me was arms possession, but I didn't have any arms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said you were beaten. Where were you beaten? That is --

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: At the police station. I can prove that. I have photos with me and the Council for Human Rights also has possession of such photos.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, can you describe for us the injuries that you suffered as a result of this beating?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: You can see the injuries in the photos I have with me.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, why -- maybe you could describe it first. Were you -- are the injuries on your head, on your body?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: On my head, on my -- all over my body. There were five policemen who bartered [as interpreted] me for five or six hours in succession. They broke two or my ribs.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said it happened at the police station. Police station where?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: In Shtime.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long were you held in Shtime?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Five or six hours I believe.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you -- were you put in jail at some point for a longer period?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It was the end of 1997 when it happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court what happened, why you were put in jail?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It was because of a personal conflict I had with a villager. They bet [as interpreted] my brother and a cousin of mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you also involved with the -- is it -- the translation we got is "bet my brother." Is it beat?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Beat, I'm sorry. It's my mistake. Beat.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you to the translator.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you involved in this fight that you have referred to?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And were you then detained by the police as a result of this fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How long were you held?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: They held me for a month in jail, but when that happened, the incident happened, it was in my home.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You mean the fight occurred in your home?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, were others held in jail as a result of this fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: My brother and my cousin were also in jail.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What about the members of the other family? Were any members of the other family put into jail as a result of this fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: For the moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did there come a time later when they were put into jail as a result of this fight?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. It came later.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It must have been November or December 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry. When were you put into jail as a result -- when did the fight occur?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After doing my jail sentence I was released, and together with my brother we went to Shtime in a shop there. When we heard those persons came and hit us behind our back -- they hit me with an axe twice in the head and they beat my father very badly and broke two of his ribs. From that moment on -- I don't know about them, I think they were arrested. I don't know any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. But the time that you were in jail was when? Again in 1997?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I was in jail. I have with me the document to -- and the document that shows my release from prison. I think it was sometime in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. I don't think I need to ask you anymore questions at this time about that subject. Lieutenant, you described how you were -- in May or June of 1997 you were taken to the police station in Shtime and beaten. Do you know if other people in your village had similar treatment by the Serb authorities?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: This was not the case only with my village. All the villages in Kosova have been subjected to such treatment. People have been brutally beaten. I'm talking in this case about my village, in Carraleve, where about 80 per cent of the villagers were submitted to this treatment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was this -- was the pretext for this treatment always searches for weapons or were there other pretexts?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: They used other pretexts as well, but the main one was of arms possession. In fact, we didn't have arms but that was only a pretext for them to maltreat the people, for them to leave Kosova.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, just to jump ahead a little bit in time for a moment. During the summer of 1998, let's say June and July of 1998, did -- during that time period did the Serb authorities try to get information about the KLA from Albanians?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They conducted investigations.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you tell us, if you know, how would they try to get -- how would they try to get information? What would they do?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: They stopped the people on the streets, they asked them if there are KLA soldiers, how many are they, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you know if they brought people to the police stations and interrogated them?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, they did. They tried to question them whenever -- wherever they could, in the streets, at the police station. People went there to have something to ask for a document or something, and then they questioned them.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, I'm going to move to another topic, and that is I want to ask you about the LDK. Were you at one time a member of the LDK?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I was. When the LDK was formed in 1989/1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you left the LDK?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After I saw its programme, I refused to remain a member in this party.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did that happen?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After two or three months, after its formation I think in 1990.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was it about the programme of the LDK that caused you to leave the LDK?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Because the programme provided for a peaceful solution to the Kosova question through dialogue, which for me was not the way to follow.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell us why that -- why you didn't find that the right solution?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Seeing what policy the Serb people were following, I thought that the programme that the LDK had was not the right one to solve the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After you left the LDK, did you join any other organisations?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: For a year I didn't join any organisation. In 1992, I became a member in the movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was the name of this movement?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The movement was for Kosova. I have with me the registration card. In 1998, I became a member of UNIKOMB. I was the chairman of the branch, the local branch, in the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What is UNIKOMB? Can you tell us what that is?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: UNIKOMB planned to protect the people and homeland by all means. And it envisioned also the use of force to protect the people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was UNIKOMB a part of the KLA or was it a separate organisation?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know that the KLA existed when the UNIKOMB was in existence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell me again the year you became a member of UNIKOMB?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It was in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Okay. We had a mistranslation there. How long were you a member of UNIKOMB?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Until the end, until the war broke out. It is while -- that period that I was in Germany.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you were in Germany during that period, were you involved at all in any organisations related to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I didn't have time to engage in such things because I used to work in two shifts. I worked 16 hours a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, you told us that you returned to Kosovo in May -- you believe in May of 1997. Do you remember when you first heard about the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. I heard about the KLA for the first time when Halit Geci was buried.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when that was?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I think it was 1997. I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was it after you returned to Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you tell the witness to stand closer to the mike, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, the interpreters need you to sit a little bit closer to the microphone to hear you. I have to ask my question again. Was this funeral after you returned to Kosovo in 1997?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Can you -- can the interpreters speak in a louder voice. I can't hear them very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that better? Can you hear better?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yeah, it's okay now.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If you have any problems hearing or understanding again, please let us know. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll try the question again. Was the funeral after you returned to Kosovo in 1997?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. I think it was the end of 1997.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember where the funeral was?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know where it was, but I know that it was broadcast on television and that we heard about the KLA for the first time.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what happened at the funeral related to the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I did not take -- attend that funeral, but I only saw on television that members of the KLA appeared there wearing masks.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After that date, did you start to read about the KLA in the newspapers?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I'd like to join them, but it was late that the opportunity rose for me to do that. I didn't read the press very regularly and I didn't dare to go to the city or to Shtime, to go anywhere for that matter.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you first hear about the KLA in your area, in around where you lived, around Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't remember the accurate date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember approximately? Was it in 1997? Was it in 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't remember accurately, as I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you yourself join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you join?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: 20 April 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you tell the Court where you went to join the KLA?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I went to Kroimire and it was the first time on the 20th of April, 1998, that I became a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Why did you go to Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Because as of 1992 I had -- I was in touch with Luan. And in cooperation with them, I managed to go to meet them, talk with them, and to become a member.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You mentioned Luan. What was Luan's real name?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Ramiz Qeriqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what village is Luan from?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: From Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You said you knew Luan in 1992. I take it you knew him by his real name, Ramiz Qeriqi, at that time in 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you see Luan when you were in Germany?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I visited him twice.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was he also in Germany?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, can you explain to us what happened in April of -- on the 20th of April, 1998, with Kroimire and Luan?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: What do you mean what happened? I don't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: My question was unclear. I'll try to ask a better question. Did -- was in -- on the 20th of April -- before you joined the KLA, was Luan already a member of the KLA? Do you know?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I didn't know, even though some friends had told me that Luan has joined. But I didn't know what Luan stood for.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your testimony is that you didn't know that Luan was Ramiz Qeriqi.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I didn't know. He had come from Germany and he had joined. I didn't know that he had joined, actually, the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what is it that caused you to go to Kroimire to join the KLA? Why did you think you could join the KLA in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It was the only hope we had to prevent the assimilation of our people.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you went to Kroimire on the 20th of April, 1998, what did you find? What was there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We found some friends; there were in uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was there a headquarters or a point established there at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: There was room there in a village -- in a villager's home, oda as we say.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And my question is: Was it established as a headquarters or a point at that time when you went to join?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I'm saying again that it was an oda, a room that is, where I met with them. I registered my name there, they gave me a weapon, and we stayed there for two, three days.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who did you register your name with?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Luan, that is Ramiz Qeriqi.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did he give you a weapon?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What kind of weapon?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: An automatic rifle, A-47 [as interpreted].

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you get a -- did you get a pseudonym at that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: My pseudonym existed from the time of the movement.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: From 1992?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what was your pseudonym?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Besniku.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you get a uniform?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No, there wasn't any.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you get a uniform -- did you somehow get a uniform later?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Later I equipped myself with uniform personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were you given any badges, KLA badges, for the uniform?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was that when you joined the KLA, in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Not on that day when I joined, but later on I got the emblem as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember when?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: About approximately?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Since I took the oath here, the truth is I really don't know what is the exact date.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But my question is: Do you know the approximate date, the month? Was it in April? May? June?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Perhaps in May, sometime like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, you said you stayed in Kroimire for two or three days. Where did you go after that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After that I became the person in charge of the point in Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did somebody tell you that you would be the person in charge of the point in Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: In agreement with Luan, I went there.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What was Luan's position in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I can't call it a position. There wasn't a special position. We did have cooperation between us, and at that time he had several positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What were they, the several positions?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: For that moment at that time there were Shukri Buja and Luan. Both of them were like persons in charge of the positions in Kroimire, of the point in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And was that in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: On the night when I went there on the 20th of April I found them there. We spent some time together at the oda. We discussed things.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You told us that Shukri Buja and Luan were persons in charge of the positions in Kroimire. I just want to know what date that was. Is that in April of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I will repeat it again. On the 20th of April, I went to Kroimire and there I met Shukri Buja, Luan, and several other friends. I don't know what their responsibilities were, but the important thing for me was that I had cooperation with Luan.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, you testified that at some point Shukri Buja and Luan were in charge of the positions in Kroimire. And my question is: When was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: To my opinion, this is my opinion, and that is that both of them were persons in charge of the points in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And in your opinion what date were they both in charge of the position?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: From the day when I went there I thought that they were the persons in charge, from 20th of April. This is my opinion. It's not that I saw a written or heard an oral order or decision.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand your testimony. Now, lieutenant, you said that you -- a few days after you joined the KLA, you became the person in charge of Petrastica. Were you responsible for any soldiers there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: How many soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Six.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And can you tell the Judges what your responsibilities were in Petrastica. What did you do there?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I stayed illegally in that house for over a month.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: In which house did you stay illegally?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: In the house where I stayed with my soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: That's a house in Petrastica?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did you do there besides staying in the house?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We would stay in the house during the day, and at night we would work on the positions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you explain to the Court what that means, "work on the positions."

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We would open trenches starting from 10.00 p.m. and working through 4.00 a.m. We would do this work in locations that were more suitable for us.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Were those locations in Petrastica or elsewhere?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: From Petrastica to Carraleve on the main road.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, with the assistance of the usher I'm going to show you a map. It's from P001, and it's map 6. And I'd ask that it be put on the ELMO, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's map 6, but it doesn't have the infamous red box on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, if you could look to your left, the usher will show you. You can look at the map there and we'll be able to follow on the computer screen. Do you recognise this map? Have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I'm going to ask first if you could take a pen and circle the village of Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Can I write on it?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Yes, please do.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I will draw an approximate line. This is approximately the Carraleve border line.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If the record could reflect that the witness has drawn a circle that encompasses what's marked as Carraleve on the map.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And then, Witness, if you could -- Lieutenant, if you could just underline where Petrastica is.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It's here.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the record could reflect that the witness has put two lines under the dot that is next to Petrastica.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where is Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: [Witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And finally, the record could reflect the witness has put a dot next to Kroimire -- Krajmirovce.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, while we have this map up here could you tell the Court in April or May 1998, which villages was the point at Kroimire responsible for in this area?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: As for April, I don't know now whether to describe that part where it exactly was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, let me ask you this: Did it change from April to May?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: There were changes on a daily basis.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, let's focus then, if you would, on -- in May of 1998. Can you describe for us or tell us the villages that came under the responsibility of the point in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I will only answer for myself, for my positions, where I know exactly how many villages it comprised. I don't know about the Kroimire point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, why don't you tell us first what villages your area comprised.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The area that belonged to the point where I was a person in charge I will tell you now about that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I underlined the four positions that we had. These are the positions that we defended.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, if the record could reflect that the witness has made two markings on -- along the road between Petrastica and Carraleve and two markings on the road between Carraleve and Dulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Witness, did there come a point -- at some point did you learn what areas were under the responsibility of the Kroimire point?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I know you don't know exactly, but can you tell us approximately what it was in your opinion.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Approximately after June, so approximately parts that were comprised in the battalion - I will call it battalion although it wasn't battalion at that time - it was Sokoli point 1 and Sokoli point 2, Petrastica point.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And where were those located? If you could put a 1 and a 2 where those were located.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: This is approximately the line for the period after June or July. Again, I say it's approximately how it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the record could reflect that the witness has drawn actually a line that goes up from the road between Carraleve and Shtime up towards Vrshec though not all the way to Vrshec and then to the west, to Kroimire and then to the south, around back to the road between Carraleve and Dulje.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, do you know if the village of Vrshec or later called Blinaje later came under the responsibility of Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: A part of the village, not the entire village.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And I see that you did not include Shale or Sedlare in the area. Was that not included under the responsibility of Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I don't know. I really don't know. I was not responsible for these things. And besides this fact, I approximately showed you where it was.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand and I am grateful for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: If this map could be given a number, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Lieutenant, you said that -- you told us that when you were staying in this house in Petrastica you were responsible for six soldiers and that you -- during the night you worked on digging trenches.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you get any help in digging the trenches or was it just you and the six soldiers?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We were assisted by the population, especially with the younger part of the population.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And during this time period, did you -- when you would work at night, did you wear masks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did there come a time when you stopped wearing masks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The masks, we carried them -- I speak for myself now. We carried them until sometime in June, 14th of June.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: After the 14th of June, did you stop wearing the masks?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I used the mask and I used my pseudonym just for the security of my family who were still in the village. The police and the army were moving around my village, and the reason for me using the mask and my pseudonym Besniku was for them not to kidnap my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: But after the 14th of June, were you able to stop wearing the mask?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: As the number of soldiers increased and we got a little bit stronger in manpower, it was not necessary for me to carry the mask any longer.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And that was the 14th of June, approximately?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: During the first fightings in Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'll ask you some questions about those in a moment. But still focusing on the time period of end of April and May and early June of 1998, did you stay in that position in Petrastica during that time?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did the number of soldiers that you were responsible for change over that time period?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The number increased on a daily basis. We had lack of weapons. A lot of young men were there to join, but we had lack of weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: By the middle of June, let's say, how many soldiers were you responsible for?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: On the 17th of June, I had 17 soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Lieutenant, during the months of May and June up until the first fighting in Carraleve, did you receive orders from somebody?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We would discuss matters with Luan and bring decisions. If it was good for us, we would carry out that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Who made the final decision after the discussions?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After the discussions, the decisions that were for our good, own good, that's what would be carried out: opening of new positions, defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So the decisions pertained to the digging of the trenches and positions that you would take. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And during May and June of 1998, what was -- what was Shukri Buja's position in Kroimire and what was Luan's position in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know what their position was. I know that they were the persons in charge of the point. Now, who exactly out of these two was, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you at one time think that one was in charge and one was the deputy?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know at around what time, but in the beginning it was like that. But when it was determined in the course of the war that Shukri Buja was commander and Luani his deputy, I don't know -- I don't know at what period of time this happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was that before the first fighting at Carraleve?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand you don't know exactly. I'm asking approximately. Do you believe -- in your opinion, was it before -- sometime before the first fighting in Carraleve, which was in the middle of June of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I know that Shukri Buja was there until the Zborce offensive took place. I thought that he was in charge there and that Luan was his deputy.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the Zborce offensive was at the end of July/beginning of August 1998. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: 25th, 26th of July.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, when you drew the diagram on the map of the area that fell under the responsibility of the Kroimire point, you included the positions in Petrastica and Carraleve.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You've told us that you would have discussions with Luan about the digging of trenches and positions that would be taken.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: My question now is: Who would make the final decision if that was required? Was it Luan who would make the final decision about these matters or was it you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: For several matters I would decide myself. For example, for opening new positions, digging trenches, I would decide for these matters myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And would you inform Luan about these decisions?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We would discuss this and this matter should be done, and I should work on this and this trench. And he would say, Go on, work.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, during this time period that we're talking about from May until the end of July of 1998, did Luan ever give you orders?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It happened that he gave me orders as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When he gave you orders, did you follow those orders?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It wasn't quite an order. It was more of an agreement. It wasn't an order in writing or told to me orally, that you should do this and this. This is how we worked together.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, do you understand the difference between an order and an agreement?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I know the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you have now testified that you received orders from Luan and that you also reached agreements. Did both things occur?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When you received an order, my question is: Did you follow the order?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, can you tell us if you remember what did these orders pertain to?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: They pertain to the defence of the existing positions so that they would not be penetrated by the Serb forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And how would Luan communicate these orders to you? Did he do it face to face? Did he call you on the telephone? Did he send somebody to tell you?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: We didn't have a phone. We would meet. Occasionally he would come to my place and sometimes I would go to his.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, Lieutenant, in your mind who did you believe was giving orders to Luan at this time period?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't think that there was a person giving an order. Depending on the situation, he would decide for himself. He would bring decisions regarding those matter that were related to the population in the area where we operated.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you believe that at times Luan was receiving orders from somebody else? Did you -- in your opinion or your belief at the time?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I rise to object. I believe that question at this juncture has been asked and answered.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Guy-Smith. I think there is enough movement in position to justify the matter being explored a little further.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, do you remember the question or should I repeat it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Repeat it, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I will. My question is: Did you believe that at times during May, June, and July of 1998 there was - and we're focusing on your belief at the moment - that at times somebody was giving orders to Luan?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Maybe later, but for that time being I don't think that there was a person giving orders for the area where we operated, because we were familiar with the territory where we operated and we knew exactly where to dig a trench. And for this area, it was Luan's decisions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did there come a time later when you believed that somebody was giving orders to Luan?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Later on, yes, I believed that he was communicating with someone, was cooperating with someone, to carry out duties that were for the best for all.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was that person?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know who he spoke to, who he agreed with. I never asked him, Who gave you orders or who did you speak to?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you ever form a belief about who was giving orders to Luan?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Well, I didn't believe to that extent that there was a person giving orders to him. This is for the beginning, but later on after the battalions were formed, I think that is the path it took by cooperating with each other and in agreement with each other.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The discussion that we had with the ICTY investigators, we did discuss certain matters. And I said that certain things are not clear. The summons was given to me for this interview, and from the 18th of August, 1998, as I said in the interview, that's when the brigades were formed.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, Lieutenant, since you brought up the interview I'm going to ask you: Do you recall in the interview saying something about who was giving orders to -- in your belief, who you believed was giving orders to Luan?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: As I said, the interview was not clear about certain matters. As for the Nerodime zone, we cannot speak about a zone because the zone did not exist at the time. And the same thing goes for the battalion. We cannot call it a battalion because it did not exist at the time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is that a convenient time do you think?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: It's an excellent time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will resume at 4.00. We'll have a break now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just raise --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: Yes, I'm sorry. I'm a little to your right, off screen perhaps. A matter which I have raised with the Prosecution in the interval so they know the point I wish to make. We have a considerable concern, at least those of us on behalf of Mr. Limaj have a concern, about the nature of some of the questions. It's a theme with this witness and it has been with other witnesses, and it is a question which begins with the words either "what is your opinion" or "what is your belief?" Now, in a large number of jurisdictions such a question would not be relevant or admissible unless the issue for the Tribunal relates to the belief of a witness, in other words what was in his mind. The reason why they're normally regarded as irrelevant or inadmissible questions is a fairly straightforward, namely it allows for speculation, to say the least of it, and material which I appreciate as a Tribunal you can evaluate and ignore. But it might save time so that you don't have to go through that exercise if, we would submit, a different form of questioning was pursued which is entirely proper. And that is to ask the witness whether he knew - and I'm going straight to the point, the point that we're on about here - is whether he knew who was giving, if anyone was, giving any commands, orders to Luan. That's the point we're on at the moment and that's been asked several times. Now, either he knows or he doesn't know. And if he doesn't know, the answer would be: Yes, I do know, because he knows there were orders and furthermore he knows who the orders were being given by. If he knows the answer to either of those two parts of the question, he can then be asked for the basis for that knowledge. The knowledge can be acquired in a number of ways. He may have been present when the person who gave the order gave the order or he may have seen a document from the person providing the order or he may have been told by Luan himself that he's getting his orders from X, Y, or Z. Now, those are all perfectly sensible routes. However, it's been taken the other way around with a general question: What is your opinion? Well, we would submit it's quite irrelevant to ask him his opinion at this stage. In fact, his opinion in our submission would never become relevant if this procedure was adopted. And our concern therefore is that when the Prosecution don't get the answer which I anticipate they hope to get, they persist in using the same language in order to attempt to get something that he may have said on a previous occasion in answer to a similar question which we would also submit is not the proper way of proceeding in order to get reliable material before Your Honours. I've taken a little time to develop it, but it's a principled objection to this form of question and I would ask that a different form is adopted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: I join in those remarks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: So do I.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, gentlemen. Indeed, Mr. Nicholls --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: You'll just have to accept my standing apologies in these matters.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I do, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: I've even written Nicholls, shows how it's getting. Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the rationale for the distinction that Mr. Mansfield presses which is perhaps true in his jurisdiction, my jurisdiction, and perhaps Your Honours' jurisdiction as well is not that it would lead to speculation but that it's a concern about hearsay and hearsay is not an issue at this Tribunal. The problem with putting the question the way Mr. Mansfield wants us to put the question is that it is too narrow, and it is my experience with witnesses such as this based on their understanding of language and their cultural understanding, that if you put the question that way, "Do you know," something they know is something they have seen for themselves or they have seen an order for themselves or something that they know directly. That is how that is understood. And of course, one can come to know something, as Mr. Mansfield himself has offered, many different ways. And therefore I am attempting to ask the question more broadly to include those other ways that one may come to know something, either by hearing about it, by dreaming about it, whatever the way is that one comes to know something. I'm of course a bit facetious there. But the point is: Once the question is answered, it can then be explored what the basis is for this belief that the witness has. Therefore, the next question of course, if it's not from me it will of course be from Defence counsel, what is the basis for this? Why did you believe this? Was it because you heard it? Was it because you saw an order? Was it because you witnessed it? My concern in putting the question the way Mr. Mansfield wants me to put it is it will foreclose those other avenues of knowledge that could be very relevant to the Tribunal and to this proceeding. I am also noting that I am attempting and I hope I have succeeded in putting the question as what he believed at the time, not today, but what he believed at the time. At least that's what my -- I've tried to do. And if I haven't done that, I can certainly be more clear in that regard.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Whiting. Mr. Mansfield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MANSFIELD
utterances.text: May I just quickly take up a couple of points. The reason why the question wouldn't be admissible normally, we would submit, is of course there is the problem of hearsay but in fact I'm not addressing the question of hearsay because strictly speaking the example I gave is hearsay. In other words, if he spoke to Luan and Luan told him, that's hearsay. But I'm not -- I haven't objected to that and I'm not objecting to it on the basis of hearsay. I'm objecting to it on the basis of speculation. I know the example was perhaps a fantastical one, but it is one that was given whether it's on the basis of a dream. I don't suppose for one moment that that is going to be proposed to be the basis. But it just shows you the ambit of possibilities here that once you ask that question in that way -- you may have had a vision of who was in charge at that time. It really doesn't matter whether you had a vision or what you had. The fundamental question you start with is "Did you know?" If it's necessary to ask the witness what he understands by the word "know" -- although given this witness so far he appears to be articulate and intelligent in his own language, and therefore one imagines that when translated the word is perfectly well understood to him -- If he says, "I didn't know," then we would submit that's the end of it, that anything less than that is not going to help you. Because as a Tribunal you're trying to assess who in fact was in a command position vis-a-vis the central issues, not who some witnesses think might have been. They, we submit, may be fuelled by all kinds of thoughts and so on. I appreciate the question has been carefully timed and is addressing the period you're dealing with, which again to which one takes no objection. Plainly, if he said "I do know" and it then arose the knowledge came later, that would be a matter for you, Your Honour, and your fellow Judges to assess. But we haven't got anywhere near that. So I think I've made the point as clear as I can, and I would ask -- we've had the witness out during this debate so he shouldn't be influenced by it, but I think the question can easily be put and clearly be put in any language.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you, gentlemen. The difficulties are obvious to all. From a legal point of view, clearly they're founded in an admixture of hearsay and potential speculation. We are not of course in a common-law jurisdiction; and hence the real foundation for the objection doesn't have that sure footing. The reality is that the difficulty is to find a way of tapping into the witness's reservoir of knowledge and understanding about a subject when words that we are used to have from what can be seen a different, precise understanding in the minds of the person being questioned. And I think it's fair to say, as was said by Mr. Whiting, that it's apparently a narrower understanding than we are used to. I think, therefore, in the circumstances questioning such as that which has been attempted should not be ruled out. If there can be a tapping of that reservoir of understanding, further questions can then lay bare whether there is some reliable basis for that understanding or not. And the Chamber can then either place some measure of reliance upon what is said or have to leave it aside as no real assistance. So while understanding the concern, particularly given the legal culture from which Mr. Mansfield comes, in this situation I think what is being done is probably an appropriate way and as good a way as can be found of trying to get the witness to speak of what it is the witness knows. Understanding may be another word instead of opinion or belief. What is your understanding? I don't know whether it will have any better result. It would be less -- it would do less immediate and obvious violence to the viewpoint of common lawyers. But nevertheless I think that is enough to indicate the position. Thank you very much for your assistance, gentlemen, but on that basis and for those reasons the approach may be persisted in.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I think the witness can be brought back in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, before the break I was asking you a series of questions about who, if anybody, was giving orders to Luan during the months of May, June, July of 1998. Do you recall those questions?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I do not.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Well, let me put it to you again just so that it's clear and we take this subject up again. During May and June and July of 1998, did you -- at that time did you think that there was somebody who would give orders to Luan?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you think that there was somebody that was above Luan who was consulting with him about what he was doing, again during May, June, and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you saying you don't know or you don't remember?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know who gave the orders. I know that they cooperated, as I did myself, with Luan. Maybe he cooperated with someone else, but I know no more.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Let me try this subject a different way. During this same time period, May, June, and July of 1998, were you aware of a general headquarters of the KLA in the area that was above the point at Krajmirovce?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Some things became clear to me after I found the card, the membership card, in the battalion from Selihu, Ruzhdi Selihu.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When did you find that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I found that after meeting -- the meeting I had with you, when I made the statement to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what did that card have on it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It is written there that this is issued to a member of Ruzhdi Selihu's soldier. It is dated 18th August, 1998. I have it with me. If you want, you can have a look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I want to focus on the time period -- is there -- what else is written on the card? It says -- actually, I would like to see the card if you could produce it.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I will, immediately. This is the membership card of Ruzhdi Selihu's battalion. And from this date I think the -- this battalion was formed. Until then, they were called points, like I said earlier, Sokoli 1, Sokoli 2, and others.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I would ask -- I'm sorry, Usher. If the usher could show the piece of paper to the Defence, please. I don't know if Your Honours also wish to see the paper. But I'll continue with my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Which is the issue? Are we to see it or in the? It's in the hands of counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand. I don't think at this time there's a need for the Bench to see it, and I'll proceed with my questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, I'm not at this point asking about the battalions. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: What I'm asking is: During the months of May, June, and July of 1998, did you think that there was a general headquarters in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: If you allow me I will say here what I think, only what I think, about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: The formation of the army resembles the building of a house. You cannot build a second floor without building the first floor. As I said, they started with the formation of the points, like Sokoli 1, Sokoli 2, and then they went on with the formation of the battalions, then the brigades, and then the operational zones.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: The points, you've testified, started to be formed as of April of 1998. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. I was in Sokoli 2 point in Pjetershtice. Sokoli 1 was in Kroimire.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And you were the commander you said of the point in Petrastica, Sokoli 2?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And your testimony is that Luan or Shukri Buja was the commander of Sokoli 1 in Kroimire?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry to rise. I don't mean to interrupt. As far as the Defence bar is concerned we would indeed invite Your Honours to look at this document, but it's Mr. Whiting's witness at the moment so I'll hand it back to him. We'd certainly like you to see it at some stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We compose ourselves in patience and await eventualities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: There's a response to that, but I just can't think of it at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: During May, June, and July of 1998, were you aware of other points in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I didn't used to move much about, so I didn't know much.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I understand and I appreciate that answer; however, my question is: Were you aware of other points in your area?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I heard about Celiku 1, Celiku 2, and things like that, but I don't know where they were located.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You don't know where Celiku 1 was located?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No. I told you, I didn't move about from my position, so I have no knowledge of that. I heard about Guri 1, Guri 2, I think.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And did you hear where those were located?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear about those during the months that we're talking about, May, June, and July of 1998?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know exactly when I heard about them. I believe it was a little while prior to the formation of the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When do you believe was the formation of the battalions, just so that we can fix that date?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I think it followed the same path that Selihu's battalion followed, that is in August.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: So your testimony is that you think you heard about Celiku 1, Celiku 2, Guri 1, Guri 2 before that. Is that your testimony?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, a little while before the formation of the battalions.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Now, the question I want to put you again is: During these same months, May, June, and July of 1998, did you hear about a general headquarters that was above these points that was responsible for several of these points?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Not in those months.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: When do you think you heard about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: After the formation of the brigades. I can't give you an exact date. And it was in Klecka.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear who the commander in Klecka was?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I can't give you the time, but it was Fatmir Limaj.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Did you hear that before the offensive at Zborce?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you sure?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I am sure because I based this on some documents I have found. When I said earlier that there are some shortcomings in my statement, that is what I meant.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Can you explain that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes. I'm explaining to you that the witness statement I made before you was a general statement. I didn't go in some specific details. That's why I'm saying here that there was not a general commander at that time or a zone commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Do you remember what you said in your interview about when there was a general commander of this area?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I said that there was a general commander, but I didn't give you any time when he was the general commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Are you certain about that?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, I'm certain.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher I'm going to show the witness ERN U003-3748. A colour copy of this has been provided to the Court and to the parties. With the yellow marking on it. I'm sorry?

utterances.speaker: MR. GUY-SMITH
utterances.text: The yellow is the colour?

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Last I checked, yellow is a colour.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Witness, could you put that -- or could the usher please put that on the ELMO. Lieutenant, do you recognise this?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm going to draw your attention to the upper right-hand corner.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And if the usher could make it visible, the upper right-hand corner. There.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Is that your signature on this map?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes, it's my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the date on there appears to be 25 April 2003. Was that the date that you signed it?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Was this an exhibit to your interview with the ICTY?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Lieutenant, who drew that line in yellow?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I drew it.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And what is this area that is drawn in yellow on this map?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: It is our zone, but I didn't specify the time when that was. In addition to that, I said that even though I am drawing this here, this is an approximate drawing. It's not an accurate one.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: You do not remember specifying a time of this area that you drew?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know the time when this zone was within this circle that I draw -- drew. I drew it as it was by the end of the war, not by the beginning of the war.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And the -- so your memory is that you drew this representing the zone at what time period?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: By the end of 1998, early 1999.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: And who was -- who was responsible for this area?

utterances.speaker: RAMADAN BEHLULI
utterances.text: I don't know the time. It was Mr. Fatmir Limaj. It must have been after August I think, as far as I remember. I'm not certain about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm going to have to ask that the witness be excused for a moment to address the Court on a matter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes. Would you wait outside for a moment, please. There's a matter that has to be debated by counsel.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would ask that we go into private session for this discussion so that the matters are not later communicated to the witness before he finishes his testimony. I would have no objection to it later being made public. My concern is that if the testimony goes into tomorrow, my concern is that these discussions get communicated to him. And I don't think that would be appropriate for the reasons that we have excused him from the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Very well. Private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We will adjourn now to resume at 10 minutes to 6.00, and we'll hear your response, Mr. Whiting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Mr. Topolski.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honours, there is a matter that I should like to raise. I've given Mr. Whiting notice of it --

utterances.speaker: MR. WHITING
utterances.text: I'm sorry --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: We'll give him an opportunity to reply, and we shall go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOPOLSKI
utterances.text: Your Honour, it is in specific --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: We're sorry to have delayed you so long. An issue is in the process of being dealt with. When you were speaking earlier in the course of your evidence, you did indicate that you had come across some additional documents that assisted you with your evidence. One of them was with the card as to your membership of the KLA. Were there other documents that you have with you that affected your understanding of your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have some notes which I have at home, but I don't have them with me now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Is it the case then that the only documents you have with you relevant to your evidence is the one that you have shown, that card. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PARKER
utterances.text: Thank you very much.
